content.intro: Learn customizing the admin interface through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Customizing the Admin Interface matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines customizing the admin interface as part of django admin. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: Customizing the Admin Interface
content_blocks.code:
from django.urls import path
from . import views

urlpatterns = [
    path("items/<int:item_id>/", views.item_detail, name="item-detail"),
]
content_blocks.expected_output: The route converter passes an integer item_id to the named view.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Open a local project using the documented Django 6.1-compatible Python environment. If this snippet depends on model names, URL configuration, settings, or an optional package, add those prerequisites before running it. Otherwise inspect it as a static example. CodeLeaf browser preview does not execute Django/Python server code.
content_blocks.troubleshooting: The view and project include() wiring must exist; URL conversion does not perform authorization or database lookup.
